rules.title: Measure BB - Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Cap
rules.requirement: Berkeley limits how much a landlord of a fully-covered rental unit can raise the rent each year through the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), and Measure BB caps that increase at a maximum of 5% even if the CPI-based formula would allow more.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to fully-covered rental units under Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, generally most units in multifamily properties built before 1980 and certain single-family homes with tenancies beginning before 1996; government-subsidized units may be fully or partially covered depending on subsidy type and HUD mortgage status.
rules.exemptions: New construction units (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980), most single-family homes and condominiums, and units with certain federal subsidies (e.g., Section 202/811, project-based Section 8 with HUD-insured mortgages) are only partially covered and not subject to the rent ceiling/AGA.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the unit is government-owned or -subsidized (e.g., Section 8, LIHTC, VASH) and whether the project has a HUD-insured mortgage, which determines full vs. partial coverage; also whether tenant shares kitchen/bath with landlord who resided there first (exempt in that case).

rules.conflict_note: The text does not give a specific effective date for the 5% AGA cap itself, only that Measure BB passed in the November 2024 election; other related provisions have specific effective dates (e.g., Dec 20, 2024 for tenant rights notices, Feb 6, 2024 for utility charge rules).

rules.title: Measure BB - Just Cause Eviction Changes (Nonpayment Threshold, Lease Breach, Notice Requirements)
rules.requirement: In Berkeley, tenants in covered units cannot be evicted for nonpayment of rent unless they owe at least one month's Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit; landlords can no longer evict for failing to sign a new fixed-term lease; eviction for lease-breach requires that the breach actually harm the landlord and that tenant behavior be shown to be unreasonable; and termination notices must direct tenants to the Rent Board and be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction threshold: 1 month's Fair Market Rent (FMR)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units exempt from the Rent Ordinance (e.g., certain new construction, most single-family homes/condos, certain federally subsidized units) are not covered by these just-cause protections.
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the unit is government-owned/subsidized and whether tenant shares kitchen/bath with a landlord who resided there first (affects exemption status).
